thread.title: Dow Jones Holds Gains: Intel, Cisco, 2 FANG Stocks Show A Key Market Leadership Trait | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Dow Jones Holds Gains: Intel, Cisco, 2 FANG Stocks Show A Key Market Leadership Trait | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD
text:
U.S. stock indexes gave back some gains after a sharp rebound Monday, even as the put-call ratio once again appeared to be pegging the low. Intel ( INTC ), Cisco ( CSCO ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) continued to show rising relative strength lines.
X The relative strength line, shown in blue on all IBD charts and in MarketSmith , gauges a stock's performance vs. the S&P 500. A rising line points to outperformance.
The Dow Jones industrial average rallied more than 1.5% at midsession Monday, but was up as much as 2.1%. The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 surged 1.2% to 1.3%. The small-cap Russell 2000 rose about 0.8%.
Volume in the stock market today was slightly higher on both major exchanges.

Please contact customer service CLOSE If the stock market continues to rise from Friday's lows, the put-call ratio will have proved prescient once again. The secondary gauge measures fear in the market. When the ratio closes at 1.15 or higher (it closed at 1.25 Friday), a short-term market low is often established.
See the put-call volume ratio in IBD's Psychological Market Indicators section.
The last two times the gauge reached those levels were on Feb. 9 and March 1, when the ratio closed at 1.26 and 1.17, respectively. The rebound was more impressive after Feb. 9 than it was after March 1.
Areas To Watch Another item to watch is the S&P 500's test of its 200-day moving average. The S&P 500 closed a whisker above the line Friday and rebounded nicely Monday. Failure at the 200-day line would be a bad sign for the market.
The Nasdaq appears to be testing the 7000 price level, but the index is comfortably above its 200-day line.
Among IBD's 197 industry groups, only six groups fell. Drugmakers and hospitals lost about 1.5% each, while losses were trivial elsewhere. On the upside, desktop software, chips and superregional banks scored strong gains.
Widely held issues also were advancing. Gainers included chipmaker Intel, up 3.5%; leisure play Netflix, up 2%; Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKA ), 1.9%; Apple ( AAPL ), 1.6%; Amazon, 1.5%; and Cisco Systems, 1.7%.
Facebook ( FB ) dived 3% on news that the Federal Trade Commission has an open investigation into Facebook's privacy practices.
Financial News The Chicago Federal Reserve's National Activity gauge rose 0.88 in February vs. expectations for 0.05. The gauge identifies growth above or below trend. Readings above zero point to growth above trend.
The Dallas Fed's manufacturing index for March rolled in at 12.7, down from the previous month's 27.9 reading. Zero is the break-even level. Readings above zero point to growth.
